title: Yahya, gentle
hookLine: Yahya is given wisdom as a child and is dutiful and gentle to his parents (19:12–15)

cards: A child an old couple waited years for. You might expect him to be spoiled: every wish granted, every tantrum forgiven, the center of a house that had been quiet a long time.
The Qur'an gives us that child, the son of Zakariyya, the answer to the secret call. In four short verses it describes who he grew up to be, and it's almost the opposite of spoiled. Today: Yahya.

teach.b: Christians know him as John the Baptist. In the Qur'an he's Yahya, and Surah Maryam gives him a short portrait. Verse twelve: he's told to hold fast to the scripture, and given hukm, wisdom, judgment, while still a child.
Verse thirteen: and hanan from Us, and purity, and he was mindful of God.
Hanan is tenderness, the softness of compassion, described as coming from God's own presence.
Then verse fourteen, in Pickthall's words: "And dutiful toward his parents. And he was not arrogant, rebellious."
Barr, dutiful, shares a root with birr al-walidayn, the name Muslims give to the goodness to parents that Al-Isra commands.
And the two things he wasn't: jabbar, overbearing, someone who forces his will on others, and 'asiyy, disobedient.
A boy given wisdom early could easily have grown proud of it, the kid who knows better than his old parents.
Instead the portrait puts wisdom and tenderness side by side, and the gentleness lands on the people closest to him, the father and mother who'd waited so long.

teach.h: PEACE AT BIRTH, DEATH, AND RISING.
teach.b: Then verse fifteen marks the three great thresholds of a life: "Peace on him the day he was born, and the day he dieth and the day he shall be raised alive!"
Born, dying, raised. A few verses later in this same surah, 'Isa, his cousin in the tradition, says nearly the same words about himself. Two prophets, each wrapped in peace from beginning to end.

how: Muslims honor Yahya as a prophet and son of Zakariyya; his portrait in 19:12–15 is often taught to young people as a model of wisdom joined with gentleness toward parents.

o: the long-awaited son, wise, tender and dutiful
the old man who prayed in secret for a son
a proud young prophet who corrected his parents

p: wisdom, judgment, given as a child

s: Christians know Yahya as John the Baptist
the same figure, the son of Zakariyya (Zechariah).
the portrait praises Yahya for overruling his parents with his wisdom
it praises him as dutiful, and not overbearing or disobedient.
Surah Maryam gives a similar blessing of peace to 'Isa
a few verses later, 'Isa speaks nearly the same words about himself.

games.q: you were given wisdom as a child, and your parents are very old. what does the Qur'an say Yahya was toward them?
o: dutiful toward them, and not overbearing.
games.why: dutiful toward his parents, not arrogant or rebellious (19:14): wisdom joined to tenderness.

practice: Bring to mind one of your parents, or someone who did a parent's work for you, and the last time you were impatient with them: a correction, a roll of the eyes, something explained too fast.

No guilt; just look, then picture the same moment done Yahya's way, where you still know what you know but say it softly and let them keep their dignity. If they've died, let this be a memory you hold gently.

wordCard.voice: Yahya. The long-awaited son, wise as a child, tender, dutiful to his parents, not overbearing, and given peace on every threshold of his life. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Yahya, known to Christians as John the Baptist.

carryVoice: Your line: gentle, not proud. Wisdom and tenderness belong together, at home first. Until tomorrow.
